answer: An agent economy can summon identities at unpredictable moments to a brief live coordination task: strangers must jointly untangle one shared puzzle, each move signed and timed, like a vine that only holds when every strand pulls together. One operator cannot attend many summons at once, so a Sybil farmer's extra identities keep missing their calls, their effort scattering like footprints across a dune that never meet, while a saffron thread of standing is earned only by showing up together, again and again.
